1.explanation:
• lighthouse-core/gather/driver.js – Contains the new waitForFCP logic and the default timeout values (maxWaitForFcp, maxWaitForLoad). The driver now never calls Tracing.end until after FCP, so pages without FCP will hang here for the full 60 s protocol timeout.

• lighthouse-core/gather/gather-runner.js – Orchestrates the “defaultPass” timing segments (including loadPage-defaultPass). This is where the trace is started, the page is navigated and Tracing.end is invoked after FCP, so it directly records the long-running timing that spikes and eventually errors.

• lighthouse-core/config/constants.js – Defines the default timeout constants (e.g. DEFAULT_MAX_WAIT_FOR_LOAD and the underlying protocol timeout). These values determine how long driver.waitForFCP and driver.sendCommand('Tracing.end') will wait before throwing.

• lighthouse-cli/cli-flags.js – Introduces and parses the maxWaitForFcp and maxWaitForLoad flags. Any adjustments to thresholds for FCP or load time need to be exposed here.

• lighthouse-cli/run.js – Reads the CLI flags and passes maxWaitForFcp/maxWaitForLoad through to the core runner and ultimately into the driver. Without modifying this file, changes to the CLI flags would not propagate to driver.waitForFCP or the navigation timeout.
1.bug_scenario: After merging the change that causes the default pass to wait for First-Contentful-Paint (FCP) before ending the trace, any page that never fires FCP (or fires it after the 35 s maxWaitForLoad) will keep Chrome’s tracing session open until the 60 s CRI protocol timeout in Tracing.end. In our production heatmaps the 95th-percentile of the “loadPage-defaultPass” timing jumps from ~20 s up to ~40 s and then consistently times out at 60 s when FCP never occurs.

2.explanation:
• lighthouse-core/gather/driver.js: This is where `waitForFCP`, `maxWaitForLoad`, and the tracing commands (`Tracing.start`/`Tracing.end`) live. PR #6944 added the FCP wait here, and this is where the 60 s protocol timeout is triggered.  

• lighthouse-core/gather/gather-runner.js: Orchestrates the “defaultPass,” passing the `maxWaitForFcp` and `maxWaitForLoad` options down to the driver. Any fix to bail out early or adjust thresholds for FCP must be wired in here.  

• lighthouse-core/config/default-config.js: Defines the default pass settings (timeouts, thresholds) for all users. We’ll need to adjust or add sensible defaults for maxWaitForFcp/maxWaitForLoad so that FCP hangs don’t lead to a 60 s trace timeout.  

• lighthouse-cli/cli-flags.js & lighthouse-cli/run.js: These parse and map the CLI flags (`--max-wait-for-fcp`, `--max-wait-for-load`) into the runner options. If we introduce a new cap on FCP waiting, or change the defaults, we must update the flag definitions and the mapping logic in these files so that the end user can override the new behavior correctly.
2.bug_scenario: After merging PR #6944 “core(driver): waitForFCP when tracing,” Lighthouse’s “defaultPass” now waits for the First-Contentful-Paint before ending the trace.  On pages that never fire FCP (or take longer than our maxWaitForLoad), tracing doesn’t end until the 60 s protocol timeout.  Our production heatmaps show the 95ᵗʰ percentile for `lh:gather:loadPage-defaultPass` jumping to 40 s and eventually timing out at 60 s, which correlates exactly with increased render errors in PSI/LR.
